strengths: Compelling and well-motivated core insight: Instead of relying on a globally fused 3D representation that inevitably accumulates cross-view pose and depth drift into noisy geometry, AnchorWeave maintains clean per-frame local geometric memories and learns to reconcile cross-view inconsistencies within the video diffusion network.

Principled architectural and algorithmic design: The greedy, coverage-driven retrieval efficiently selects complementary viewpoints along target camera chunks, and the multi-anchor weaving controller elegantly integrates shared multi-anchor attention with pose-guided importance fusion.

Strong and thorough empirical validation: The method outperforms both single-anchor methods and global/implicit memory baselines (including Gen3C, EPiC, SEVA, SPMem, and Context-as-Memory) across PSNR, SSIM, and VBench perceptual metrics on DL3DV and RealEstate10K.

Extensive diagnostic and ablation analyses: The paper and appendix provide comprehensive ablations on global vs. local memory, number of anchors, attention strategies, efficiency scaling with history length, and extreme long-horizon explore-and-revisit stress tests (up to 2,400 frames).
weaknesses: Baseline re-implementation caveats: Key directly comparable memory-based approaches like SPMem and Context-as-Memory are not publicly available and were reimplemented by the authors on CogVideoX. Although standardizing the backbone aids comparison, performance differences may partially stem from implementation nuances.

Inference and memory overhead: Processing multiple anchor videos (e.g., $K=4$) via the 3D VAE and running joint attention over concatenated anchor tokens increases computational and VRAM requirements (e.g., runtime increases from 221s to 275s and memory from 34GB to 39GB on an RTX PRO 6000), making real-time or streaming usage challenging without aggressive optimization.

Heuristic handling of dynamic scenes: The framework assumes static scene geometry for point-cloud memory construction. Dynamic objects currently require external foreground segmentation and masking, meaning native spatio-temporal dynamics and out-of-sight state persistence are not yet handled end-to-end.

Sensitivity to upstream monocular 3D estimation: The quality of rendered anchors is bottlenecked by the external 3D/depth estimator (TTT3R), showing vulnerability in scenes with strong view-dependent reflections or severe pose drift over long trajectories.

strengths: Compelling and well-motivated core insight: The paper accurately identifies that fusing multi-view point clouds into a single global 3D memory inevitably accumulates registration and depth estimation errors (leading to ghosting and geometric distortion). Replacing global 3D fusion with a bank of clean local geometric memories and delegating cross-view reconciliation to a learned neural module is an elegant and effective design choice.

Well-crafted architectural and algorithmic components: The coverage-driven retrieval greedy algorithm systematically maximizes visible coverage along target camera chunks, avoiding redundant anchor selection. Furthermore, combining shared multi-anchor attention with pose-aware importance fusion allows the model to effectively resolve residual cross-view discrepancies.

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: The method is validated on standard benchmarks (RealEstate10K, DL3DV) across two modern diffusion backbones (CogVideoX-5B and Wan2.2-5B). It outperforms or matches strong competitive baselines (such as SEVA, SPMem, and Context-as-Memory) across reconstruction metrics (PSNR, SSIM), camera control precision (rotation/translation errors), and perceptual quality benchmarks (VBench).

Thorough ablations and diagnostic analyses: The ablation studies clearly isolate the impact of each design decision, including global vs. local memory representations, pose-guided vs. uniform anchor fusion, joint vs. separate attention, and anchor budget scaling. The long-horizon revisit stress test (up to 2,400 frames) and runtime scaling analysis provide valuable practical insights into the system's behavior.
weaknesses: Primary reliance on static scene assumption: Because local memories are represented as rigid 3D point clouds extracted via a monocular 3D estimator (TTT3R), the framework assumes a mostly static physical scaffold. While dynamic elements are demonstrated via character masking (Section H.3), general in-the-wild dynamic scenes with moving background elements or topological alterations remain challenging without explicit auxiliary dynamic tracking modules.

Computational and memory footprint of multi-anchor processing: Retaining and encoding $K$ anchor videos expands the sequence length in the shared attention block to $K \times L_a$. Although the authors show that inference remains feasible (e.g., Table 4), processing multiple anchor latents alongside the diffusion backbone incurs noticeable latency and VRAM overhead compared to simpler single-stream conditioning models.

Error propagation in autoregressive write-back: In the long-horizon update–retrieve–generate loop, newly generated video segments are re-projected into 3D and appended to the memory bank. As noted in the failure analysis, any visual hallucinations or depth/pose inaccuracies in generated frames inevitably degrade future retrieved anchors over extended exploration horizons.

strengths: Compelling core motivation: Replacing brittle, globally fused 3D representations with clean, per-frame local geometric memories effectively sidesteps the ghosting, drift, and accumulated misalignment common in long-horizon global 3D reconstructions.

Well-designed technical framework: The combination of coverage-driven greedy retrieval (maximizing incremental FoV coverage) and the Multi-Anchor Weaving Controller (leveraging shared cross-anchor attention and pose-guided fusion) offers an elegant, learnable mechanism to reconcile residual multi-view discrepancies.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The paper benchmarks against a strong suite of recent camera-controllable and memory-based baselines (including SEVA, SPMem, Context-as-Memory, Gen3C, EPiC) across RealEstate10K and DL3DV, demonstrating solid quantitative gains in reconstruction (PSNR, SSIM) and perceptual metrics (VBench).

Thorough ablations and diagnostics: The paper provides informative ablations verifying each design choice (global vs. local memory, pose-guided vs. average fusion, shared vs. separate attention, and anchor count K), along with an extensive appendix analyzing efficiency scaling, extreme revisit stress tests (up to 2,400 frames), and failure modes.
weaknesses: Dependency on upstream 3D estimators: While local memories prevent multi-view fusion drift, the system remains reliant on the accuracy of monocular depth/pose estimators (e.g., TTT3R). In scenarios with severe scale ambiguity, complex lighting, or textureless regions, poor initial geometry can propagate errors into the generated anchors.

Computational overhead and memory footprint: Running joint attention over K anchor latents incurs tangible memory and latency costs (increasing generation time from 221s to 275s and peak GPU memory to 39 GB at K=4 on Wan2.2-5B), which may constrain its applicability in interactive or resource-constrained settings.

Limited handling of scene dynamics: The method is inherently formulated around static 3D world geometry. Dynamic foreground elements require pre-segmented masking or external monitors (as discussed in Appendix H.3), meaning dynamic scene modeling remains an open challenge rather than an integrated capability.

Quantitative validation is predominantly short-to-medium horizon: The primary quantitative evaluation uses 70-frame sequences (21 context frames, 49 target frames). Although Appendix H.2 includes a qualitative/PSNR stress test over thousands of frames, broader quantitative metrics on dedicated long-horizon navigation benchmarks would further strengthen the empirical findings.

strengths: Clear motivation and insightful approach: Addressing the error accumulation and ghosting artifacts inherent in globally fused 3D scene representations by switching to clean per-frame local 3D memories and delegating cross-anchor reconciliation to a learned controller is well-reasoned and technically sound.

Well-structured framework: The pipeline combines a coverage-driven greedy retrieval algorithm, shared multi-anchor cross-token attention, and relative-pose-guided importance fusion into a cohesive architecture that effectively integrates multiple geometric anchors.

Strong experimental evaluation: AnchorWeave is evaluated on two prominent backbones (CogVideoX and Wan2.2) across standard benchmarks (RealEstate10K and DL3DV) against a comprehensive set of competitive baselines, demonstrating superior temporal smoothness, perceptual quality, and camera controllability.

Thorough ablations: The experiments convincingly isolate and validate each component, including local vs. global geometric representations, shared vs. separate attention, pose-guided fusion, and the retrieval budget K.
weaknesses: Lack of inference efficiency and computational overhead analysis: Encoding K separate anchor videos through the 3D VAE and concatenating their tokens inside the controller's attention blocks (K * La tokens) inevitably increases memory footprint and inference latency. The manuscript would be strengthened by reporting runtime, FLOPs, and GPU memory overhead during generation compared to single-anchor and global-fusion baselines.

Handling of dynamic scenes: The system relies on static scene geometric priors (e.g., TTT3R point clouds). While Section F discusses masking out dynamic actors in specific game-like settings, the method fundamentally assumes mostly static environments, and a clearer discussion of failure modes and bounds on dynamic object handling would be beneficial.

Discussion on SEVA trade-off: In Table 1, SEVA achieves a marginally higher PSNR than AnchorWeave (21.13 vs. 20.96 on CogVideoX and 21.04 on Wan2.2). While AnchorWeave outperforms SEVA on SSIM, VBench temporal smoothness, and temporal flicker, a deeper analysis comparing the trade-offs between SEVA's multi-view conditioning and AnchorWeave's explicit anchor rendering would add valuable context.

strengths: Insightful and well-motivated concept: Replacing a single, drift-prone globally fused 3D point cloud with multiple retrieved local geometric point cloud memories effectively sidesteps the compounding registration/depth errors of long-horizon 3D reconstruction, shifting the burden of multi-view reconciliation into a learned generative controller.

Well-designed technical architecture: The coverage-driven greedy retrieval algorithm ensures maximum FoV coverage along target trajectory chunks without redundancy, while the multi-anchor weaving controller neatly combines shared cross-anchor attention with relative-pose-guided importance weighting and explicit target camera guidance.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Strong quantitative results against a wide suite of state-of-the-art baselines (e.g., ViewCrafter, Gen3C, TrajCrafter, EPiC, SPMem, SEVA) on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, achieving favorable trade-offs between geometric consistency (PSNR/SSIM) and temporal video quality (VBench smoothness/flicker).

Thorough ablations and qualitative validation: Ablations systematically dissect the impact of local vs. global geometry, pose-guided vs. average fusion, shared vs. independent attention, and anchor count K. The extensive qualitative results on long-horizon keyboard navigation and open-domain loops demonstrate robust consistency.
weaknesses: Computational and inference overhead: Concatenating latents from up to K rendered anchor videos and processing them through shared attention blocks (scaling token length by a factor of K) incurs non-negligible computational and memory overhead. The paper would be strengthened by reporting wall-clock inference latency, throughput, and peak GPU memory compared to single-anchor or global-anchor baselines.

Sensitivity to upstream depth/pose estimation quality: Although local point clouds avoid global multi-view drift, they still rely on monocular pose and geometry prediction (TTT3R). The paper does not thoroughly analyze the failure modes under severe scale ambiguity, depth noise, or poor camera pose tracking.

Scope primarily limited to static environments: The core formulation assumes static scene geometry. While Section F demonstrates a dynamic third-person character scene by masking the character out from point cloud construction, this remains a heuristic workaround rather than a principled treatment of dynamic 4D scene memory.

Benchmark diversity: Quantitative benchmarks are restricted to camera walkthrough datasets (RealEstate10K and DL3DV). Testing quantitative performance on datasets featuring more challenging motion or outdoor unstructured environments would further strengthen the claims.

strengths: Clear motivation and well-justified problem formulation: The paper clearly identifies a fundamental bottleneck in existing 3D-conditioned video world models—namely, that accumulating multi-view observations into a globally fused 3D representation inevitably compounds pose and depth estimation errors, leading to ghosting and floaters. Replacing global fusion with clean, per-frame local geometric memories is an intuitive and effective solution.

Well-designed technical architecture: The proposed pipeline is coherent, featuring a principled coverage-driven greedy retrieval algorithm to select complementary geometric anchors, alongside a multi-anchor weaving controller combining shared cross-anchor attention and camera-pose-guided importance fusion.

Thorough empirical evaluation: AnchorWeave is evaluated on standard benchmarks (RealEstate10K and DL3DV) across both reconstruction fidelity (PSNR/SSIM) and perceptual quality (VBench), comparing favorably against prominent baselines (SEVA, SPMem, Context-as-Memory, Gen3C, etc.).

Model generality across modern backbones: The framework is demonstrated on multiple recent DiT-based architectures, specifically CogVideoX-5B and Wan2.2-5B, demonstrating adaptability to state-of-the-art open-source generative models.

Comprehensive qualitative and ablation evidence: The ablation studies in Section 4.3 (Table 2, Table 3, and Figure 5) convincingly isolate and validate each component's utility (local vs. global memory, shared vs. independent attention, and pose-guided fusion vs. naive averaging).
weaknesses: Computational and memory overhead at inference: Encoding and attending over K anchor video latents via shared attention inevitably increases memory and latency costs during denoising. The manuscript lacks quantitative runtime, latency, or peak GPU memory profiles comparing single-anchor vs. multi-anchor generation.

Long-horizon memory bank scalability: Storing uncompressed per-frame point clouds and associated poses as memory indefinitely can lead to significant storage footprint over extremely long horizons (e.g., thousands of frames). The paper does not explore memory retention, pruning, or hierarchical keyframe selection strategies.

Assumption of static environments: The pipeline relies heavily on static point cloud reprojection via TTT3R. Although Appendix F shows a heuristic where dynamic characters are masked out in a third-person setting, handling complex object motion and topological scene changes remains fundamentally challenging for purely geometric anchor rendering.

Marginal reconstruction gains over strong implicit baselines: In Table 1, the reconstruction metric gains (PSNR/SSIM) over SEVA are relatively modest (e.g., SEVA achieves 21.13 PSNR / 0.6711 SSIM compared to 20.96 / 0.6727 for CogVideoX and 21.04 / 0.6739 for Wan2.2), although perceptual and temporal metrics show clearer separation.
